raw_response:
I am 50 years old, been farming 12 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years. I finished middle school. My household is just me and my wife — 2 people total. We have a well for irrigation, and I split my land into 8 mu for wheat followed by maize, and 4 mu for cotton. That is what I did last year, and I am not changing it unless something forces me to.

For the 8 mu of winter wheat, I will buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — about 12.5 kg per mu. Before sowing in October, I will spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. The bag says 16-16-16, so that gives about 8 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Then in March at green-up, I will top-dress with one 25-kg bag of urea per mu, which is about 11.5 kg nitrogen. At jointing stage in April, another half bag of urea, about 6 kg nitrogen. So in total that is roughly 25 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate 3 times: once around New Year for winter water, once at jointing, and once at heading if the weather is dry. I will spray pesticide twice — once when I see aphids, and once for powdery mildew if it shows up. I will do rotary tillage before sowing. Last year I got 470 kg per mu; this year I expect about 480 kg per mu if the frost does not come late.

For the summer maize on the same 8 mu, I will plant hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrid now, the old types are not worth it. I hire the no-tillage seeding machine right after wheat harvest because there are only about 10 days between harvest and sowing, no time to plough. At sowing I put down one 40-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Then at big trumpet stage, I side-dress with one 25-kg bag of urea per mu. That comes to about 22 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate 3 times — at jointing, big trumpet, and grain filling. The well water costs electricity, but summer rain is not reliable enough to skip it. Pesticide twice. I expect 550 kg per mu. Last year was 530, so I am hoping for a bit more.

For the 4 mu of cotton, I will use improved cotton seed. Cotton is hard work, but the price was decent last year so I kept these 4 mu. I plough the cotton field in spring because cotton roots need loose soil. I apply about 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu — cotton needs more potassium for the bolls, I learned that from the input dealer and from watching the neighbors. I buy one bag of potassium chloride extra for the cotton field. I irrigate 3 times. Pesticide 4 times because bollworm and aphids are trouble on cotton, and I would rather spray one extra time than lose the bolls. I expect 240 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I worry about costs every year. Urea is over 100 yuan per bag now, compound fertilizer is even more. For 12 mu I need dozens of bags. But I learned my lesson years ago — cutting fertilizer to save money is gambling with your harvest. My neighbor Liu cut back two years ago and his wheat turned yellow and thin. He lost half his yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a bit of fertilizer is just a cost you absorb. I watch what my neighbors do. If the people around me are putting two bags of urea on their wheat, I put two bags. If they are spraying three times, I spray three times. That is my science.
